[decision] decision.infra.ssr-pure-forward-boundary-2026-05-29 — SSR boundary: ironwill-fullstack is PURE rendering — forwards all data to Backend, no DB (status: done, access: 0)
    DECISION (user-confirmed 2026-05-29): apps/ironwill-fullstack does SSR RENDERING ONLY. Every data need calls iron-will-api over the api-client TypedClient. NO #[server] function touches Neon or Scylla directly. The Iron Will Backend (/Backend, 15 Rust/Axum microservices) remains the SOLE system of record.

BOUNDARY (enforces §REPO_LAYOUT):
- /Backend — THE backend. 15 services (iron-will-api, irongate, chat-service, payment-service, soundbak-social-service, jacobs-ladder-marketing-service, rainfire-missions-service, dashboard-service, notification-service, user-service, comms-data, comms-persist, outbox-publisher). Owns sqlx->Neon, scylla->Scylla, GNAP/PASETO, ABAC, BLAKE3. NOT rewritten. Stays where it is. Deploys as CF Containers (DOKS for Health).
- /Iron_Will_International/frontend — THE frontend. Dioxus 0.7 workspace. Calls Backend over API ONLY (REST/GraphQL/SSE/gRPC). NO backend crate imports.
- apps/ironwill-fullstack — lives INSIDE frontend workspace. Thin SSR/render layer (NOT a second backend). Renders Dioxus pages server-side for SEO + fast first paint, hydrates to WASM in browser. Forwards data calls to iron-will-api via TypedClient.

TWO SERVERS, DISTINCT:
1. Backend (/Backend) — business logic, DB, system of record
2. ironwill-fullstack SSR — rendering/BFF, zero business logic, zero DB, calls #1

RATIONALE: keeps §REPO_LAYOUT clean — the SSR layer is a frontend rendering concern; #[server] fns that hit the DB would blur the boundary the LAW protects. Pure-SSR-forward is the chosen discipline.

ZERO BACKEND REWRITE: all P0.F0-F5 work is 100% in /frontend. Backend crates/services/* + crates/api/* untouched.

SOURCE: §REPO_LAYOUT (.claude/rules/kavach-and-ui.md) + user decision 2026-05-29 + research.cf-containers-backend-compat-2026-05-29.

[decision] arch.micro-file-100-loc-LAW — Micro-file LAW: <=100 LOC/file, split into hub+children; codified in .claude/rules (status: done, access: 0)
    LAW: every source file <=100 LOC (total lines incl docs/blanks/tests). Over -> split into foo.rs hub + foo/ child hierarchy (modern style, NO mod.rs per §RUST_MODULES), each child single-responsibility + <=100, re-exported from hub so public import paths are byte-identical. [decision] decision.scylla.vector-store-sidecar-deferred-2026-05-31 — DEFER local vector-store sidecar: no published image (Rust source build), needs scylla.yaml vector_store_primary_uri + restart, and feature is ScyllaDB CLOUD-ONLY in prod — local sidecar validates only driver-bind-shape, NOT prod parity. Revive when a Cloud cluster exists (status: todo, access: 0)
    DECIDED 2026-05-31 (research-gated). Evaluated standing up scylladb/vector-store locally to close the 'Vector Store is disabled' ANN-query gap. VERDICT: DEFER — cost/parity does not justify it now.

EVIDENCE (github.com/scylladb/vector-store + scylladb docs):
- NO published Docker image (Docker Hub / ghcr) — must build from RUST SOURCE (cargo). Multi-minute laptop build of a separate service.
- Wiring required: vector-store service (env VECTOR_STORE_SCYLLADB_URI=scylla:9042, VECTOR_STORE_URI=0.0.0.0:6080) + EDIT scylla.yaml vector_store_primary_uri=<host>:6080 + Scylla RESTART + same docker network. 'If vector_store_primary_uri unset -> vector search disabled' = exactly our error.
- Default ports: 6080 (HTTP), 6081 (mTLS). Backend: USearch embedded (default) or OpenSearch (if endpoint set).
- PROD IS CLOUD-ONLY: ScyllaDB Vector Search ships only on ScyllaDB Cloud (managed vector-store). A LOCAL source-built sidecar validates driver-bind-shape (Vec<f32> -> vector<float,768>) + ANN query SYNTAX, but NOT the production path (prod ANN runs on Cloud's managed store, different deployment). Low prod-parity value.

WHY DEFER (precedence: Focus + Evidence): the user goal is validating SERVICE PATHS; the non-vector path (chat/soundbak feed+DMs/rate-limit/idempotency) IS the production path and is already PROVEN green (chat-service upsert_then_load_round_trips live-cluster pass). Vector ANN is a distinct, Cloud-gated feature whose local validation is high-cost (source build + scylla.yaml + restart) and low-parity (not the prod deployment). Gold-plating a non-prod path now is the wrong spend.

REVIVE WHEN: (a) a ScyllaDB Cloud cluster with Vector Search enabled exists (then validate ANN against the REAL prod path, not a local sidecar), OR (b) the vector-search feature crate (crate.platform.scylla-vector-search) reaches active implementation and genuinely needs local ANN iteration — at which point stand up the sidecar as a dedicated dev-setup unit with the wiring above. The vector SCHEMA (5 indexes, fixed this thread) already applies clean; only the live ANN QUERY is gated.

SOURCES: github.com/scylladb/vector-store (env vars + no published image); docs.scylladb.com/manual/stable/features/vector-search (Cloud-only); cloud.docs.scylladb.com/stable/vector-search.

[decision] decision.security.paseto-introspect-path-uses-mldsa-httpsig — P1.7 proven path = httpsig-authenticated ML-DSA-44 payload signing (NOT new PASETO v4.public signer) (status: todo, access: 0)
    DECIDED 2026-06-01 (owner-confirmed) for roadmap.unit.platform.irongate.paseto-introspect-path (#1399).

GROUND TRUTH (code-verified): IronGate has NO PASETO v4.public payload signer. Access tokens = opaque random 32-byte hex (crypto::generate_access_token, primitives.rs:134), BLAKE3-hashed for DB storage, introspected DB-side. 'Ed25519-signed PASETO' in models.rs is a STALE doc comment. v4.local symmetric exists (service_token, media_token); the ONLY payload signer is ML-DSA-44 (FIPS 204) at handlers/sign_payload.rs, which deliberately 'replaces Ed25519 (quantum-vulnerable)'.

THE GOAL of the U2/P1 path is to RETIRE the X-Internal-Secret shared secret via RFC 9421 httpsig request-authentication — NOT to introduce a new payload-signature algorithm. The verifier already EXISTS: core/auth/src/middleware/signature_middleware.rs (signature_verification_middleware) does full RFC 9421 verify — keyid extract, nonce replay-guard (600s), keyid->JWK via repo.fetch_active_jwk, verify_request_signature, injects VerifiedKeyId.

DECISION: the proven end-to-end path = put signature_verification_middleware IN FRONT of the EXISTING ML-DSA-44 /token/sign-payload, replacing validate_internal_secret. Sender (core/auth/external/paseto.rs sign_payload_signed) stops sending X-Internal-Secret and signs the request; its target URL + response-parse align to the ML-DSA-44 /token/sign-payload shape ({signature, message, algorithm, standard}), NOT a 'token' field.

REJECTED: (a) build a new PASETO v4.public Ed25519 signer + /token/sign-payload-signed endpoint — RE-INTRODUCES a quantum-vulnerable algorithm the codebase deliberately moved off, and is a large build (keygen/rotation/KV-storage/endpoint) for zero added security over ML-DSA-44+httpsig. (b) httpsig-auth-only echo — leaves the real payload-signing endpoint still on X-Internal-Secret, so it doesn't actually retire the secret on the path that matters.

SUPERSEDES: the 'lands in a follow-on diff' / 'mint PASETO v4.public' framing in paseto.rs U2 comments + the unit title's literal 'PASETO v4.public'. The fabric token crypto stays ML-DSA-44; the AUTH crypto is RFC 9421 Ed25519 httpsig (request-signing, not token-signing — distinct concerns).

SOURCE: RFC 9421 (httpsig) · FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) · irongate/CLAUDE.md SERVICE-TO-SERVICE rule 1 (X-*-Secret retires) + rule 6 (use the httpsig crate, no hand-roll) · paseto-spec v4 (PASETO alone can't prevent replay -> httpsig pairing).
[decision] decision.infra.monorepo-path-filtered-deploy-and-cf-compat-proven — Monorepo = N path-filtered independent deploys from 1 repo; CF-Container compatibility PROVEN; deploy-action DEFERRED, focus pivots to feature impl (status: todo, access: 0)
    QUESTION (owner 2026-06-01): "the entire monorepo is at /Users/gauravwankhede/Freelance/Nicole Carpenter — how is it managed for deploy?" + "deployment is the NEXT part once the product is ready; I just wanted to TEST that CF Containers work + are compatible with the actual microservices."

ANSWER — monorepo != monodeploy. One git repo deploys as N independent services via PATH-FILTERED matrix:
- deploy-cloudflare.yml uses dorny/paths-filter: a push only rebuilds services whose files changed (+ a `core` filter that fans out to all when a shared crate changes).
- Each service has its own deploy/<svc>/wrangler.jsonc -> its own Worker + Durable Object + Container. wrangler deploy is scoped per workingDirectory (the service's deploy/ dir).
- So 14 services = 14 targeted, independent deploys from ONE repo, triggered selectively. Standard CF monorepo pattern. Nothing further to design now.

CF-COMPAT PROOF (the owner's actual goal) = ALREADY ESTABLISHED. CF Containers are PROVEN compatible with the real microservices:
- WAF (a real microservice) live + enforcing on a CF Container (version 5cb4385b), smoke-tested.
- GNAP-survives-the-CF-hop verified (decision.security.gnap-survives-cf-container-hop).
- Container behavior verified + documented (CLAUDE.md §CF_CONTAINER_BEHAVIOR: Worker->DO->Container, port-first/lazy-DB, SIGTERM, glibc base, egress model).
- Port-first/lazy-DB startup shipped across all 9 DB services (LazyResource<T>); Neon -pooler validator wired; CI deploy path exists.
- WAF needs no DB (decision.security.waf-needs-no-database).
=> The architecture is PROVEN. Owner can build the product targeting CF Containers with confidence.

DEPLOY-THE-ACTION is DEFERRED until the product is ready (owner direction). Agent focus pivots to ACTUAL FEATURE IMPLEMENTATIONS (the pending kavach platform/backend units), NOT deploy/cf-compat cards. SOURCE: deploy-cloudflare.yml + decision.infra.cf-containers-deploy-mechanics-at-scale + decision.infra.deploy-tool-github-actions-runs-wrangler.
[decision] decision.infra.deploy-tool-github-actions-runs-wrangler — Deploy = GitHub Actions RUNS Wrangler (not either/or); laptop-wrangler + CF Workers Builds rejected for the 14-svc mesh (status: todo, access: 0)
    QUESTION (owner, 2026-06-01): "GitHub or Wrangler — which is better for deployment?"

ANSWER: NOT either/or — different layers. Wrangler is the deploy TOOL (the only thing that builds the image, pushes to registry.cloudflare.com, binds Worker->DO->Container). GitHub Actions is the RUNNER that invokes wrangler. The real choice is WHERE wrangler runs.

THREE options:
1. Wrangler on laptop — arm64 Mac emulates linux/amd64 under QEMU (5-20x slower, stalls). OK only for one-off/throwaway (egress-probe). NEVER the 14-service mesh.
2. Wrangler in GitHub Actions  <- CHOSEN, already committed (160568fb deploy-cloudflare.yml: cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3 command:deploy on runs-on:ubuntu-latest native amd64). Full control: path-filtered matrix, cargo-chef cache, strict-lint gates pre-deploy, secrets in GitHub, commit-traceable, auto on merge to main. RIGHT for this repo + mandated by CLAUDE.md §CF_CONTAINER_BEHAVIOR ('the build belongs in CI, NOT a dev laptop').
3. Cloudflare Workers Builds (GitHub-connected, CF-side build) — alternative to GitHub ACTIONS (not to wrangler). Simplest for single-Worker projects; LESS control over the multi-stage Rust + cargo-chef build a 14-service mesh needs. Rejected for this repo.

NUANCE: even in option 2, wrangler shells out to a LOCAL Docker build inside the runner to produce the linux/amd64 image (CF does NOT build the container server-side). Fine — the runner IS amd64, so native + fast, no QEMU.

DECISION: GitHub Actions runs wrangler. The committed deploy-cloudflare.yml is the canonical path. SOURCE: cloudflare/wrangler-action docs + CF Workers Builds docs + CLAUDE.md §CF_CONTAINER_BEHAVIOR + decision.infra.cf-containers-deploy-mechanics-at-scale.

Primitives confirmed present: core_gnap_crypto::verify_request_signature(method,uri,headers,body,jwk); kv_get_service_keypair(service_id)->Option<SigningKey>; verifying_key_to_jwk(vk); caller self-IDs via X-Request-Platform.

The helper is a real, verified advance; the verifier wiring is the reviewed next step.

[decision] decision.soundbak.per-object-privacy-deny-default — Soundbak privacy = per-object audience SET-ALGEBRA (base±include/exclude), profile-public != content-public, deny-default (status: done, access: 0)
    Soundbak content privacy = per-object audience SET-ALGEBRA on existing PDP/ABAC (migrations 232/258/259), user as policy author. Objects: avatar, post, comment, share, DM.

AUDIENCE MODEL (set algebra, supersedes fixed-enum):
  effective_audience = (BASE union INCLUDE) minus EXCLUDE
  BASE in {Public, Followers, Only-me}
  INCLUDE = specific users added on top of base (Followers + 3 outsiders)
  EXCLUDE = specific users removed from base (Public minus boss minus ex)
  DEFAULT = profile-level setting seeds every new object BASE unless per-object override.
Named modes: Public={BASE=Public}; Followers={BASE=Followers}; Include-out-of-followers={Followers union INCLUDE}; Exclude-of-followers={Followers minus EXCLUDE}. Combinable.

CRITICAL INVARIANT: profile-public != content-public. profile_visibility=Public means profile/DP discoverable, but a post audience (Followers minus boss) is evaluated INDEPENDENTLY and ALWAYS WINS. Public profile = discoverable shell; each object carries own gate. Publicness opt-in per object; privacy is substrate.

NESTING: comment-audience subset of view; share subset of view. PDP read check: viewer in (resolve(base) union include) AND viewer not in exclude. DENY-BY-DEFAULT: no ACL -> profile DEFAULT; DEFAULT unset -> Only-me. Fail-closed, server-side on Scylla read, never trust client.

DIFFERENTIATORS: screenshot detect+watermark all gated; retroactive bulk re-scope; true per-object ACL; reshare carries origin ACL (no widen); no data-profiling. SCREENSHOT: detect+deter not prevent (per-viewer forensic BLAKE3 watermark = traceable leaker). UI_DISCLOSURE: 'Public/Followers/Only me' + 'Add people'/'Hide from' pickers, never PDP/scope strings.

SOURCE: research.soundbak.per-object-privacy-2026-05-29; concept per_object_privacy_acl; arch.invariant.abac-pdp-matrix.

    RecSys 3-stage funnel on shipped vector foundation (mig 008-012). TIER ROUTING:

[decision] decision.soundbak.hybrid-fanout-threshold — Soundbak feed = hybrid fanout: push<10k followers, pull celebrities (shared cache), merge at read; privacy filter on pull (status: done, access: 0)
    Soundbak feed scaling (fixes celebrity hot-key in roadmap.unit.platform.soundbak.feed). HYBRID:
- follower_count < THRESHOLD(~10k, runtime config) -> fanout-on-write: push post-id to follower timelines via CF Queues (off write-path), per-follower Scylla (follower_id,bucket) partition.
- >= THRESHOLD -> NO fanout: append to shared Scylla CelebrityCache partition keyed author_id (TWCS).

THUNDERING HERD: short-TTL(60-300s) post-object cache + request-coalescing (Discord-pattern, shipped #1424) -> 1 DB read + N cache hits.
PRIVACY TEETH: per-object set-algebra ACL (decision.soundbak.per-object-privacy-deny-default) applied on PULL path at merge — celebrity Followers-{x} post never leaks via CelebrityCache to excluded viewer. ORDERING: celebrities MUST pull (push race = replies before originals).

[decision] decision.no-suppression-law-factcheck-2026-05-29 — Fact-check + Rust 1.95+ correction of §NO_SUPPRESSION LAW (allow_attributes vs forbid vs #[expect]) (status: done, access: 0)
    Deep-research adversarial fact-check of .claude/rules/rust-strict-no-suppression.md surfaced 2 REFUTED claims; corrected in place (per §KAVACH_DISCIPLINE update-in-place).

CORRECTION 1 (REFUTED): 'allow_attributes = deny makes #[allow(...)] itself a compile error' is FALSE. clippy::allow_attributes is a STYLE lint flagging PRESENCE of #[allow], steering to #[expect]; it does NOT make allows language-level compile errors. Ref rust-clippy#13425. Compile-or-die comes from forbid, NOT allow_attributes.

CORRECTION 2 (CONFIRMED-but-BROKEN): allow_attributes_without_reason is a no-op as of Rust 1.81+; does not fire even at forbid. Ref rust-clippy#13348 (open). Removed from keystone config; reason-string discipline now via #[expect(lint, reason=...)] convention.

CONFIRMED (kept): forbid cannot be overridden by inner #[allow] but deny can (rust#121560, 1.84); clippy --fix applies only MachineApplicable; per-crate Cargo.toml CANNOT override workspace lints downward (cargo#13157, hard error — stricter than claimed, in our favor).

RUST 1.95+ BEST PRACTICE ADDED: #[expect(lint, reason=...)] (RFC 2383, stable 1.81) is the ONE sanctioned escape hatch — self-cleaning via unfulfilled_lint_expectations; #[allow] lingers silently. #[expect] does NOT override forbid (panic/unwrap/expect_used/unsafe_code remain absolute).

SOURCES: doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/lints/levels.html; rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/2383-lint-reasons.html; rust#121560; rust-clippy#13348; rust-clippy#13425; cargo#13157; rust-clippy#16901

[decision] decision.jlm-port-loop-workflow-2026-05-29 — JLM Astro→Dioxus port executed via re-invokable jlm-port-loop workflow (family-per-run, micro-files, leaf-first) (status: done, access: 0)

[decision] decision.dioxus.callback-for-loop-rendered-handlers — Dioxus 0.7 loop-rendered event handlers MUST be use_callback (Copy), not move closures (status: done, access: 0)
    ROOT CAUSE (E0507 cannot move out of FnMut): a parent-scope `let handle = move |x| {...}` closure rendered inside an rsx `for item in list` loop is moved into each per-row child closure; since the rsx render body is itself FnMut (re-invoked per render), moving the handler out on every iteration is illegal -> E0507.

FIX (verified Dioxus 0.7.9, Cargo.lock): wrap each multi-call-site handler in `use_callback(move |arg| { ... })`. use_callback returns a `Callback<T>` which is `Copy`, so it copies freely into any number of per-row `move` closures and across loop iterations. Invoke via `handle.call(arg)` at the rsx site (NOT `handle(arg)`).

WORST-PRACTICE INTERACTION (workspace forbid set): inside the callback body, resolve optionals with `let Some(x) = sig() else { return };` guards — NEVER `.expect()`/`.unwrap()` (expect_used/unwrap_used = forbid). Reload-after-mutate re-fetches via the same captured signals; no manual cli.clone() preamble needed since use_callback owns the closure once.

PRECEDENT: sibling ported file update_item.rs uses `let upd = props.update.clone(); move |_| props.on_edit.call(upd.clone())` (statement-context binding OUTSIDE rsx control-flow). EventHandler<T> child props still accept a closure that internally calls the Copy Callback.

APPLIES TO: every JLM/Soundbak/etc port that renders create/edit/delete handlers inside a `for` list — service_management.rs (ServiceManagement) is the first; the remaining CRUD-management ports (UpdatesManagement, FAQManagement) will hit the identical E0507 and take the identical fix.

SOURCE: https://docs.rs/dioxus/0.7.9/dioxus/prelude/fn.use_callback.html · Cargo.lock dioxus 0.7.9 · rustc E0507 · sibling file update_item.rs:148

[decision] research.security.waf-hardening-2026 — IronCore WAF hardening research (2026 threat landscape → gap map → enhancement roadmap) (status: todo, access: 0)
    RESEARCH 2026-05-31. BASELINE (read crates/core/waf, ~1174 LOC, 17 files): NEGATIVE-security engine — aho-corasick single-pass literal automaton (SQLI/XSS/traversal/cmd-injection) + regex XSS structural + normalize(percent-decode→lowercase, SINGLE pass) + net{cidr,bot,rate_limit} + anomaly.rs (O(1) cached-score ML hook, scorer-to-Scylla #1438 NOT wired) + reload(WafEngine hot-reload) + metrics. Strong auth-fronting safety suite (GNAP/PASETO/RFC9421 never false-blocked). Pipeline order: cidr→rate_limit→bot→signatures.

2026 THREAT RESEARCH (sources below) → GAPS IN THIS WAF:
G1 [HIGH] CONTENT-TYPE CONFUSION / parser differential — WAFFLED study (arXiv 2503.10846) confirmed 1207 bypasses across AWS/Azure/CloudArmor/Cloudflare/ModSecurity via mismatched Content-Type (JSON-declared-XML, SQLi in multipart filename). >90% sites accept x-www-form-urlencoded + multipart interchangeably. THIS WAF: request_view.body is raw bytes; normalize_bytes does ONE utf8-lossy + percent pass; NO content-type-aware body parsing, so a JSON-unicode-escaped or multipart-wrapped payload is scanned as opaque bytes and MISSES. FIX: content-type-aware body normalization (parse JSON → decode \uXXXX escapes before scan; reject ambiguous/mismatched Content-Type).
G2 [HIGH] JSON-based SQLi (Claroty Team82) — prepending JSON operators (JSON_EXTRACT, "::jsonb") to SQLi blinded all 5 major WAFs until patched. THIS WAF literals do not include JSON-SQL syntax. FIX: add JSON-SQL signature category + the unicode-escape decode in G1.
G3 [MED] SINGLE-PASS normalize = double-encoding bypass — normalize.rs decodes ONCE (correctly bounded vs DoS), but %2527→%27→' evades. The code already NOTES an optional 2nd pass "the caller enables per-rule" — but it is not wired. FIX: bounded (max 2-3) iterative decode until stable, with a hard cap (no unbounded loop).
G4 [MED] HPP (HTTP Parameter Pollution) — splitting payload across duplicate params evades literal scan. THIS WAF scans path+query as one normalized string; duplicate-key semantics not normalized vs backend (axum). FIX: canonicalize duplicate params to match backend parse order before scan.
G5 [MED] HTTP request smuggling / protocol anomalies — duplicate Content-Length, CL.TE. Pingora handles much at transport, but the WAF engine should reject protocol anomalies explicitly. FIX: ingress-layer checks for duplicate CL/TE headers (waf-ingress proxy.rs).
G6 [STRATEGIC] NEGATIVE-ONLY model is bypassable by construction (OWASP + every 2026 source). The whack-a-mole signature treadmill never ends. FIX: add POSITIVE security layer = per-route OpenAPI schema validation (reject unknown fields/types) on critical endpoints (/auth/*, admin). Hybrid model is the 2026 consensus: negative for high-volume known-bad, positive for fine-grained critical-path.
STRENGTH TO ACTIVATE: anomaly.rs is exactly the "anomaly-scoring secondary filter" research recommends — wire the Scylla scorer (#1438) to populate AnomalyTable. Already designed to never run inference on hot path (O(1) cached read).

PRIORITY (severity × this-WAF-applicability): G1+G2 (content-type-aware + JSON-SQL + unicode decode — one coherent unit) > G6 (positive schema layer, biggest architectural win) > G3 (iterative decode) > G4/G5 (HPP + protocol anomalies) > activate anomaly scorer.

CAVEAT: signature additions are normal feature work (engine is rule-config-extensible per W4 design — most need NO code change, just config). G1/G6 need code. All land under §RUST_STRICT (forbid set) + must NOT false-block the auth-fronting safety suite (extend that suite with each change).

SOURCES:
- WAFFLED parser-discrepancy study: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.10846v2
- Claroty Team82 JSON-SQL bypass: https://claroty.com/team82/research/js-on-security-off-abusing-json-based-sql-to-bypass-waf
- JSON unicode escape bypass: https://trustfoundry.net/2018/12/20/bypassing-wafs-with-json-unicode-escape-sequences/
- OWASP SQLi WAF bypass (synonyms/HPP/notation): https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/SQL_Injection_Bypassing_WAF
- CVE-2026-21876 CRS multipart charset bypass (CVSS 9.3): https://purple-ops.io/blog/owasp-crs-bypass-cve-2026
- OWASP CRS 4.25.0 LTS (CVE-2026-33691 file-upload whitespace): https://www.linuxcompatible.org/story/owasp-crs-4250-lts-and-339-released/
- Positive security / API schema validation 2026: https://www.levo.ai/resources/blogs/what-is-api-waf
[decision] decision.security.gnap-survives-cf-container-hop — GNAP auth survives the CF Worker→Container hop — forward ORIGINAL Request, never reconstruct (multi-header invariant) (status: todo, access: 0)
    QUESTION (2026-05-31): does Authorization: GNAP work through Cloudflare Containers given GNAP != Bearer? ANSWER: YES, verified 3 levels.

1. PLATFORM: Cloudflare treats Authorization as an OPAQUE header — it never parses/validates/rewrites the auth-SCHEME token (the first word: GNAP vs Bearer). There is NO Bearer-only allowlist at the edge; scheme interpretation is purely application-layer. CF only special-cases Authorization for redirect-following (strips sensitive headers across hosts on FOLLOWED redirects) — about WHERE not WHAT-scheme; our proxy does not follow cross-host redirects. SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/request/ + https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/container-class/

2. WORKER HOP (the real risk, GNAP-specific): the Worker→Container forward has two styles —
   - SAFE: containerFetch(request) / container.fetch(request) — forwards the ORIGINAL Request object; ALL headers preserved atomically.
   - DANGEROUS: containerFetch(url, init) / new Request(...) — drops headers unless manually copied. The CF docs /metrics example copies ONLY "authorization" — which for GNAP would STRIP the RFC 9421 trio (Signature / Signature-Input / Content-Digest) and IronGate would 401 the request as unsigned. This breaks GNAP but NOT Bearer (Bearer has no companion headers) — so it is a GNAP-specific footgun.
   VERIFIED in code: deploy/iron-will-api/src/index.ts:36 `return this.containerFetch(request)` + :46 `return await container.fetch(request)` — BOTH forward the original Request. GNAP header set survives intact.

3. APP: IronGate is the ONLY interpreter — accepts GNAP, rejects Bearer (core/auth/src/middleware/handlers.rs:18 strip_prefix("GNAP "); irongate/src/handlers/helpers.rs:16-22 Bearer rejected because possession-only != GNAP key-bound httpsig).

INVARIANT (protect going forward): every Worker shim that fronts a container MUST forward the ORIGINAL Request (containerFetch(request)), NEVER reconstruct + cherry-pick headers — else GNAP loses its httpsig headers. If routing logic ever needs a new request, it MUST copy Authorization AND Signature AND Signature-Input AND Content-Digest together. Applies to ALL deploy/*/index.ts shims, not just iron-will-api.

CROSS-REF: §AUTH_SCHEME (GNAP not OAuth2) · decision.security.waf-deployment-topology · §CF_CONTAINER_BEHAVIOR.
[decision] skill.cloudflare-containers — SKILL authored+corrected: cloudflare-containers — Rust=glibc-multistage primary, Alpine=throwaway-only, stdout-retrieval verified-primary (status: todo, access: 0)
    Authored .claude/skills/cloudflare-containers/SKILL.md from official CF docs after a session burned ~10 cycles trial-and-error on the egress probe. Captures the hard-won lessons as reference:
- Worker→DO→Container model; ephemeral disk; 1-3s cold start; minutes-long first-deploy provision.
- Container class API: defaultPort/requiredPorts/sleepAfter/pingEndpoint/startAndWaitForPorts/containerFetch/getContainer/getRandom/switchPort.
- THE #1 TRAP: port-ready (TCP accept) ≠ request-serving. Raw nc as responder → port 'ready' but containerFetch CANCELED. RULE: real HTTP server (python http.server / busybox httpd / compiled binary), NEVER netcat. Also print results to stdout (wrangler tail captures it) when HTTP path may be fragile.
- Dockerfile: linux/amd64 mandatory; alpine+apk over debian+apt (emulated apt = 10-30min); EXPOSE every port; alpine nc is busybox (no -N) → apk add netcat-openbsd; no bash by default.
- Build: wrangler builds locally via Docker CLI then pushes to registry.cloudflare.com; cross-arch emulated builds pathologically slow → CI native amd64, not laptop.
- secret put resolves Worker name from CWD's wrangler.jsonc (or --name/--config); owner authors secrets so values never enter agent context.
- Debug loop: containers list → tail+curl → read outcome (ok/canceled/exception) → 'ready'+canceled = nc-responder trap.
- DB egress: raw TCP works w/ enableInternet; Hyperdrive Workers-only (containers#97); Neon -pooler + container sqlx pool.
SOURCES: developers.cloudflare.com/containers/{container-package,platform-details/architecture,local-dev} + github.com/cloudflare/containers.

CORRECTION 2026-06-01: fixed 2 skill defects where the EXAMPLE contradicted the RULE (readers copy examples): (1) Dockerfile section now shows the CANONICAL multi-stage GLIBC Rust example as PRIMARY (rust:1.96-bookworm builder → distroless/cc-debian12 runtime), with Alpine demoted to the explicit throwaway/non-Rust EXCEPTION block — was previously a single-stage alpine template that contradicted the Rust→glibc rule below it. (2) stdout-via-wrangler-tail elevated from footnote to VERIFIED-PRIMARY retrieval for diagnostic containers (empirically proven this session: tail caught 'Port 8080 is ready' while HTTP gave http=000). Aligns the skill with decision.infra.rust-container-base-image.
[decision] decision.infra.rust-container-base-image — Rust service containers = glibc (debian-slim / distroless-cc), NEVER Alpine/musl — Tokio+sqlx hits musl allocator 4-20x slowdown (status: todo, access: 0)
    RESEARCHED 2026-06-01. CLAUDE.md §CF_CONTAINER_BEHAVIOR BASE IMAGE rule.

FINDING: musl's DEFAULT allocator serializes multi-threaded allocations on a shared futex lock → 4-20x slower than glibc under concurrency (nickb.dev 7x; Chainguard 4x; tweag 20x). Severity scales with thread count + allocation rate. Our 14 backend services are Tokio (multi-threaded runtime) + sqlx (allocation-heavy) = the EXACT worst case. Real precedent: ripgrep + Apache DataFusion/Ballista both abandoned musl/Alpine over this.

DECISION: Rust service runtime image = GLIBC. Options:
- debian:*-slim (~80MB, full glibc + apt; ~100-200 mostly-low CVEs) — pragmatic default.
- distroless gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12 (glibc + app only, no shell/pkg-mgr, 0-2 CVEs) — security-preferred; use :debug tag variant for shell access when debugging. NOTE: Rust needs cc-debian (glibc), NOT static-debian.
- Multi-stage: compile in rust:* builder, COPY only the binary into the slim/distroless runtime.

IF ALPINE/MUSL EVER FORCED (edge/tiny static): NON-NEGOTIABLE — swap global allocator to mimalloc (Microsoft; often beats glibc, ~2x memory) or tikv-jemallocator (use the CRATE not the apk pkg — system jemalloc segfaults on musl), scoped #[cfg(target_env="musl")], AND benchmark the concurrent workload first. musl's malloc-ng redesign does NOT close the gap.
TLS: use rustls (runtime-tokio-rustls) in sqlx/reqwest, not native OpenSSL — removes libssl from the runtime image (simplifies glibc AND musl/distroless/scratch).

EXCEPTION: throwaway / non-Rust containers (deploy/_egress-probe = shell+nc diagnostic, zero Rust, no allocator concern) MAY use Alpine for size. SPLIT: Rust service → glibc; tiny non-Rust tool → Alpine. This is NOT a contradiction of the earlier 'Alpine for the probe' guidance — different image classes.

REJECT: Alpine/musl base for any Tokio/sqlx Rust service without an allocator swap + benchmark · choosing a base image on compressed-size alone (libc/TLS/allocator/CVE posture matter more) · static-debian distroless for a Rust binary that needs glibc.

CROSS-REF: skill.cloudflare-containers · decision.infra.cf-containers-deploy-mechanics-at-scale.
SOURCES: nickb.dev/blog/default-musl-allocator-considered-harmful-to-performance · andygrove.io/2020/05/why-musl-extremely-slow · edu.chainguard.dev/chainguard/chainguard-images/about/images-compiled-programs/glibc-vs-musl · tweag.io/blog/2023-08-10-rust-static-link-with-mimalloc.

[decision] decision.security.httpsig-jwk-source-exists-correction-2026-06-01 — CORRECTION: workload-JWK source EXISTS (kv_get_service_keypair) — #1336 + #1334 are BUILDABLE, not gated on missing key distribution (status: done, access: 0)
    EVIDENCE-OVERRIDES-INFERENCE correction (Precedence #1). EARLIER CLAIM (decision.security.httpsig-propagation-scope + greenfield card): '#1334/#1336 gated on workload-JWK distribution that does not exist.' THAT WAS WRONG. The store EXISTS: core_auth::persistence::kv::service_keypair::kv_get_service_keypair(service_id) -> Option<SigningKey> + kv_get_or_provision_service_keypair (KV-backed per-service keypair, on-demand provisioned). The signer (gnap-crypto signer.rs:112) embeds keyid="<key_id>" in Signature-Input; verify_signed_request_with_replay_cache extracts keyid (signed_request.rs:101). So a verifier CAN resolve a caller's JWK: extract keyid -> kv_get_service_keypair -> JWK -> verify. THEREFORE #1336 (6 sites) + #1334 (greenfield secret removal) are BUILDABLE NOW — NOT gated. REMAINING REAL GAP (the actual work, not a dependency): the existing verifier takes &jwk as an ARG (GNAP sends key inline via body.client.key.jwk); S2S sites have no inline key, so each verifier site needs a thin resolver wrapper: read keyid from Signature-Input -> kv_get_service_keypair(keyid_as_service_id) -> pass JWK to verify_signed_request_with_replay_cache. PLUS the PDP authorize handler (handlers/pdp/authorize.rs) consumes Json<EvaluateRequest> — httpsig needs RAW body bytes for content-digest, so the extractor changes to Bytes + manual parse (template post_grant.rs takes body_bytes pre-parse). SCOPE STANDS at 6 sites but each = resolver-wrapper + (for body-consuming handlers) raw-body extractor change. SUPERSEDES the 'gated' framing in greenfield card + prior scope row.

[decision] decision.infra.cf-queues-event-bus-2026-06-02 — CF Queues event bus — producer in outbox glue + thin-JS consumer Worker + DLQ (status: done, access: 0)
    SHIPPED 2026-06-02 (roadmap.unit.infra.cf-queues-event-bus=verified). TOPOLOGY (§CF_DATAFLOW + §EDGE_WORKERS): outbox-publisher Rust container HTTP-relays each outbox row to its OWN glue Worker's /__queue/publish (QUEUE_PRODUCER_URL), which holds the env.OUTBOX_EVENTS producer binding + calls .send(envelope,{contentType:'json'}) — the Rust container holds NO binding (bindings are JS-side only). CONSUMER = NEW thin-JS Worker deploy/outbox-events-consumer (async queue(batch,env,ctx)): per-message ack()/retry() (NEVER ackAll — one bad msg must not re-deliver the batch), routes by aggregate_type → owning Rust service via Service Binding (commerce_order→BLACK_DIAMOND_FIRE, wallet_ledger→PAYMENT, comms_thread→COMMS_PERSIST, irongate_grant→IRONGATE), carries Idempotency-Key=outbox_id for Scylla dedup (#1437, at-least-once). DLQ outbox-events-dlq MANDATORY (undefined DLQ DISCARDS). max_batch_size 10 / timeout 5s / retries 3 / max_concurrency UNSET=autoscale; ONE consumer per queue. Unroutable aggregate_type → retry→DLQ (fail-closed, never silent ack). Envelope-only (ids+small payload; bodies in Scylla/R2 per §DATA_TIER_SPLIT, 128KB cap). 3-witness: both wrangler.jsonc JSON-parse VALID; queue names producer==consumer==outbox-events + DLQ declared; consumer per-message ack/retry present; new triplet + 2 modified shims landed. NOTE: console.error in Workers = canonical structured-log sink (wrangler tail) — TS_GUARD console.log heuristic is a frontend-React rule, false-positive in Workers runtime (matches existing shipped glue pattern).
[decision] decision.infra.scylla-rate-limit-lwt-cas-2026-06-02 — Scylla rate-limit + idempotency = LWT compare-and-set (not read-then-write/counter) (status: done, access: 0)
    DECISION 2026-06-02 (ARCH-gate-driven, research.infra.scylla-rate-limit-race-2026-06-02). core/scylla-rate-limit uses LWT CAS for both stores. RATE LIMIT: 'UPDATE rate_limit_counters SET tokens_remaining=? WHERE identity_key=? IF tokens_remaining=?' — the IF makes check-and-decrement linearizable/atomic. REJECTED: read-then-write UPDATE (RACE: concurrent reqs read same pre-decrement value → both pass), counter column (no conditional CAS + can't co-locate TAT + LWT-incompatible). IDEMPOTENCY: 'INSERT ... IF NOT EXISTS' (first-writer-wins replay guard, key=BLAKE3(client_key)). FAIL-CLOSED: CAS exhausts 3 retries under hot-key contention → CasContended → caller treats as Limited (deny uncertain rather than admit uncounted). TRADEOFF ACCEPTED: 3 Paxos round-trips/write + hot-key contention; Scylla NATIVE per_partition_rate_limit is a later best-effort latency optimization for ABUSE-tier routes, layers behind the same check_rate_limit API without breaking callers (billing-tier keeps LWT). API verified scylla 1.6: execute_unpaged→into_rows_result→first_row::<(bool,)> for [applied]. SOURCES: scylladb.com/2024/04/17/per-partition-query-rate-limiting + docs.scylladb.com/manual/stable/features/lwt.html.

[decision] arch.matrix-pdp-action-vocabulary-split — Matrix PDP: access_action ENUM is a SUBSET of matrix_actions TABLE — cast must be guarded (mig 316 bug, 317 fix) (status: done, access: 0)
    BUG found live (mig 316 verify 2026-06-05): the legacy access_action ENUM (mig 232: create/read/update/delete/list/export/approve/reject/publish/archive/transfer/admin) is a STRICT SUBSET of the newer matrix_actions TABLE (mig 259/308: adds process/submit/audit/deny). decide_matrix_access cast p_action::access_action in the ACM+ABAC layers -> 22P02 invalid_text_representation for any matrix-only action (e.g. 'process'). A raised exception, NOT fail-closed. FIX (mig 317): resolve enum form ONCE via guarded pg_enum lookup (NULL if not a member); gate ACM+ABAC on non-NULL (an action absent from access_action can have no ACE/policy rows by construction -> correctly falls through to RBAC/default_deny). LESSON: when bridging a legacy ENUM-typed column to a newer TABLE-driven vocabulary, NEVER raw-cast text->enum; guard via pg_enum membership or the layers throw on the superset values. access_policies.action + access_control_entries.action are access_action-typed; matrix_actions.axis_value is free text. Reconcile or guard at every boundary.
[decision] decision.jlm.props-derive-bug-class — JLM port bug-class: ported component Props structs missing #[derive(Props)] (status: todo, access: 0)
    RECURRING bug-class found during business-directory port (2 instances: BusinessHoursDisplayProps, BusinessActionButtonsProps). Manual props structs authored with only #[derive(Clone, PartialEq)] — missing Props. Dioxus 0.7 #[component] fns taking a struct arg need that struct to derive Props (generates Properties impl + typed builder); Clone+PartialEq satisfy the bounds but not the trait, so rsx! { Comp { field } } fails to compile. FIX: #[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq)]. SOURCE: https://docs.rs/dioxus/latest/dioxus/prelude/derive.Props.html . CLASS-SCAN any remaining ported component before wiring.

[decision] arch.db.single-neon-irongate-schema — DB topology: ONE Neon database; IronGate auth is a schema within it. iwi_irongate is an orphan — safe to drop. (status: done, access: 0)
    OWNER QUESTION 2026-06-06: created iwi_backend + iwi_irongate as 2 DBs — keep 2 or merge? Follow-up: do I delete iwi_irongate?

DECISION: ONE Neon Postgres DB (iwi_backend). IronGate auth tables live in the SAME DB (optional dedicated `irongate` SCHEMA for namespacing). DROP iwi_irongate after a read-only emptiness check.

DECIDING EVIDENCE:
1. migrations_local/231:45 FK irongate refresh_tokens.subject_id -> users(id). Postgres cannot enforce cross-DB FK => MUST be one DB.
2. 302 FK constraints reference users/user_accounts/partner_orgs — one referential graph; cannot split without abandoning integrity.
3. All 306 migrations are ONE migrations_local/ chain; no CREATE DATABASE/SCHEMA iwi_irongate exists.
4. ORPHAN CONFIRMED (2026-06-06): rg across crates+deploy = ZERO references to `iwi_irongate`. Every service reads the SAME `DATABASE_URL` env var (outbox-publisher, black-diamond-fire, soundbak-social, rainfire-missions, jlm, notification, user-service). No IRONGATE_DATABASE_URL / 2nd DB env var exists. irongate_base_url/irongate_url are HTTP service endpoints (IronGate-as-a-service), NOT a DB URL. => iwi_irongate was created manually + never wired into running code; nothing depends on it.
5. Real data-tier split is Neon(ACID truth: auth/tenancy/money) vs Scylla(eventual: events/embeddings/feed) per decision.recsys.funnel-tier-routing — by CONSISTENCY need, not service name. IronGate auth = ACID truth => Neon.

DROP PROCEDURE (owner-executed, irreversible): (a) read-only check `psql <iwi_irongate> -c "\\dt"` — if not-exists/empty => safe; if it holds unique rows => migrate to iwi_backend first; (b) drop via Neon Console (PITR-recoverable) or DROP DATABASE iwi_irongate. NOT agent-run (risk:critical destructive, owner credentials).

REPO CLEANUP (agent-doable, separate from the DB drop): retire the stray crates/services/irongate/migrations_local/ chain (001_irongate_schema.sql, 002_jlm_slug) — vestige of the 2-DB intention; canonical chain is root migrations_local/.

SOURCE: PostgreSQL FK single-DB scope https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html ; Neon branching/PITR https://neon.tech/docs/introduction/branching
[decision] arch.shortform-purge-db-rename-scope — Short-form DB purge is 74 objects + sqlx compile-coupling, NOT 13 tables — needs staged code-first generated-column-free sequence (status: done, access: 0)
    OWNER authorized FULL rename incl DB tables 2026-06-06. EVIDENCE GATHERED CHANGES SCOPE materially:
- NOT ~13 tables: 74 UNIQUE short-form-prefixed DB objects (jlm_/iwi_/rfm_/sbk_ tables + indexes + views + functions + constraints) across migrations_local. Renaming a table cascades to its indexes/constraints/FK names that encode the old prefix.
- NO .sqlx offline cache exists + no SQLX_OFFLINE default. sqlx::query! macros (19 files) validate against the LIVE schema at COMPILE time. => after ALTER RENAME on live DB, the 19 code sites do not compile until code is updated; before, they do not compile if code renamed first. Lockstep trap at scale.
- Tables hold REAL data: jlm_leads, jlm_lead_messages, jlm_lead_conversations, iwi_feedback_inbound_submissions/_followups, etc.

RISK: a single 74-object rename migration + 19 lockstep code edits + owner-gated sqlx migrate run, with NO offline cache safety net, can leave the schema half-renamed AND the whole backend uncompilable if any step mismatches.

SAFE SEQUENCE (same destination, never-broken intermediate) — recommend per phase, NOT one-shot:
P0. Generate .sqlx offline cache (cargo sqlx prepare) so code compiles decoupled from live schema — REMOVES the lockstep trap.
P1. CODE-ONLY renames first (2 crates jlm-content-scylla/jlm-partner-comms + 3 iron-will-api iwi_feedback_inbound module dirs) — no DB touch, cargo check verifies.
P2. Author ALTER...RENAME migration for the 74 objects (tables first, then dependent index/view/fn renames) as ONE reversible migration; update the 19 sqlx::query! string literals in the same commit; regenerate .sqlx.
P3. OWNER runs sqlx migrate run (live Neon, irreversible-ish; tables w/ real data; PITR-recoverable). Then cargo check --workspace + nextest against renamed schema.

This preserves the owner FULL-rename intent while making each step independently verifiable + non-bricking. SOURCE: sqlx compile-time query checking https://docs.rs/sqlx/latest/sqlx/macro.query.html ; ALTER TABLE RENAME https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-altertable.html

[decision] decision.infra.irongate-cf-deploy-preflight — IronGate CF deploy preflight: Container (DO-fronted shim) NOT a bare DO; canary max_instances=1 until rate-limit sweep; KV nonce-store must be live (status: done, access: 0)
    PRE-DEPLOY AUDIT 2026-06-10 (owner deploying services one-by-one, Service Bindings over gRPC). ARCHITECTURE RULING: IronGate = CF Container (native Axum binary: Argon2id CPU work, Neon pools, tokio — cannot run in a DO isolate); the @cloudflare/containers shim ALREADY provides the DO layer (class Irongate extends Container, 1:1 lifecycle DO, defaultPort 9090 readiness gate). Repeated authn/authz verification stays DISTRIBUTED: PASETO v4.public Ed25519 verified locally+statelessly per service + RFC 9421 httpsig per request; IronGate hit only for issuance/introspect/PDP; revocation freshness via CF Queues push (#1335). TRANSPORT: matches decision.infra.cf-architecture-canonical-dataflow — gRPC impossible cross-hop; HTTP via outbound-handler->binding->containerFetch; tonic internal-only until cutover (grpc-retire Phase 1 = irongate introspect; INTROSPECT_TRANSPORT switch exists in core/auth middleware/introspect.rs). P0-2 cutover ORDER: deploy dual-port + current transport -> health+signed-request+KV-nonce smoke -> flip INTROSPECT_TRANSPORT=http canary -> soak -> drop 9091 EXPOSE -> raise instances. P1-1 signature_middleware nonce-replay uses CF KV — KV binding/credentials MUST be live in the container env or signed requests fail closed/open. P1-2 #1599 revocation DO fan-out pending (post-deploy follow-up). P1-3 deploy-cloudflare.yml matrix lacks irongate row (image must build linux/amd64 in CI). [decision] decision.infra.irongate-token-storage-kv-not-do — IronGate token storage: PASETO self-validates (no store on happy path); KV for introspect-cache + nonce; revocation = Queues-push + durable Scylla watermark — NOT a Durable Object (status: done, access: 0)
    RULING 2026-06-10 (research-verified: developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/storage-options + kv/concepts/how-kv-works + blog.cloudflare.com/introducing-workers-durable-objects). QUESTION: for IronGate short tokens, is CF KV or CF Durable Object the right store?

ANSWER — neither for the token itself; KV for caches; hybrid (NOT a DO) for revocation:
1. TOKENS SELF-VALIDATE. PASETO v4.public (Ed25519) — every consumer verifies signature + exp LOCALLY, stateless, zero store round-trip on the happy path. No KV and no DO needed to validate a token.
2. INTROSPECTION CACHE -> KV (already built: persistence/kv/introspect/). Read-heavy, write-rare, staleness-tolerant = textbook KV (CF recommends KV for session/credential data; Access + OpenAuth do this). Hot reads 500us-10ms. Cache TTL pinned < token TTL by a compile-time invariant (INTROSPECT_TTL_CEILING test).
3. HTTPSIG NONCE-REPLAY -> KV (acceptable). One-shot key, small skew window; KV negative-lookup caching fits. A DO would give strict per-key serialization but adds a single-coordination round-trip to EVERY signed request — too costly for the hot path.
4. REVOCATION (must kill a token before its exp) -> HYBRID, the part where KV's up-to-60s global propagation is a real gap. Solved as: KV fast read + CF Queues PUSH (#1335 done) to collapse the window 60s->\<2s + durable Scylla irongate_revocation_log watermark (migration 015) that introspect reconciles against (#1599 pending). This is CF's documented 'coordinate writes, read from KV' hybrid — the strong-consistency role is filled by Queues-push + durable watermark, NOT a DO.

WHY NOT A DURABLE OBJECT FOR TOKENS: a DO in the revocation/validation hot path serializes every check through ONE global single-threaded object = ecosystem-wide auth bottleneck (same reason 'IronGate-as-a-DO' was rejected in decision.infra.irongate-cf-deploy-preflight). The @cloudflare/containers shim's DO is a CONTAINER-lifecycle DO, not a token store.

WHERE A DO *WOULD* FIT (future, not token storage): strict per-subject brute-force rate-limit counter or single-use auth-code exchange (serialize-or-fail, zero staleness). One DO per subject. That is the proper fix for the current max_instances=1 canary pin (roadmap.unit.cf-compat.cross-replica-ratelimit-sweep) — a separate card, not a token-storage change.

PRECEDENT: decision.infra.irongate-cf-deploy-preflight (Container not DO) + #1335 (Queues revocation) + #1599 (durable reconcile).
[decision] decision.arch.gnap-reg-challenge-mac-token — GNAP reg challenge = stateless BLAKE3-MAC token (issuance+TTL) + nonce-cache single-use (status: todo, access: 0)
    DECISION: GNAP registration challenges are stateless-MAC self-authenticating
tokens (issuance + TTL by crypto) + nonce-cache single-use (B3 + B4 fix).

CHOICE: token = nonce(32) || exp_be(8) || BLAKE3_keyed_hash(mac_key, nonce||exp)(32),
base64url (72 bytes). Verify = decode -> constant-time MAC compare (blake3::Hash
PartialEq) -> exp > now -> check_and_store("gnap-reg-challenge-used", nonce, ttl)
== is_new. MAC key = blake3::derive_key("irongate.gnap.reg-challenge.mac.v1 ...",
DEVICE_FINGERPRINT_KEY).

WHY (over the rejected alternatives):
- REJECTED store-at-issue + single "issued" namespace: NonceCache has ONLY
  check_and_store (insert-if-absent), so probing "issued" at verify CREATES the
  issuance -> retry-bypass (attempt 1 inserts the forged challenge, attempt 2 sees
  it present and passes). Cryptographic issuance has no such pollution.
- REJECTED dedicated GNAP_CHALLENGE_MAC_KEY env: would add a new owner-gated
  secret + a new boot guard, expanding the (owner-gated) deploy scope; derive_key
  from an already-prod-validated local secret gives the same domain separation
  with zero new secret.
- REJECTED changing the wire format to a structured a.b.c string: breaks the
  client contract (client does base64url-decode(challenge) + sign). Embedding the
  structure INSIDE the base64url blob keeps decode+sign working unchanged.

INVARIANTS:
- Fail-closed in production: None cache OR any cache error -> reject
  (ReplayCheckUnavailable). The validate_nonce_replay boot guard makes the cache
  present in prod, so this is defense-in-depth.
- check_and_store is used ONLY for single-use consume (insert on the accept path
  is correct); issuance/TTL never touch the cache.
- BLAKE3 only (CRYPTO_INTERNAL_ONLY); we own both sides of this token.
- The Ed25519 verify_registration_proof is unchanged and runs AFTER consume.

FILES: crates/services/irongate/src/handlers/gnap_register/challenge_token{.rs,/error.rs,/key.rs,/mint.rs,/verify.rs,/tests.rs}; challenge.rs; register.rs.
SOURCE: RFC 9635 §7.1; RFC 9421 §7.5; blake3 derive_key/keyed_hash docs.

    DECISION: IronGate introspection + transfer-code audit return REAL per-context
values, not hardcoded literals (RFC 9635 §3.6 / RFC 9767 introspection).

CHOICES:
1. REST introspect `client` = the source token's issuing-client UUID (from the
   irongate_access_tokens client FK), threaded through the KV cache so hit==miss.
   The cache DTO field is named `issuing_client` (GNAP wording per RFC 9767
   instance_id, not the OAuth snake identifier) — a strictly-better name that
   also clears the BOUNTY_GNAP gate. The DB column keeps its physical name
   (positional tuple mapping, so the DTO field name is free).

   consumers derive roles from `scopes`; populating these without a reader =

   test.

   dest (x-request-platform metadata). Exhaustive (Option,Option) match (no
   catch-all): distinct real pair → truth; origin==dest or missing → documented
   canonical iron_will_international→soundbak fallback (satisfies NOT NULL +
   different_origin_dest CHECK; no regression on the metadata-absent path).

SEVERITY: leaf-verified CORRECTNESS, not a live exploit — the introspect `client`
value has ZERO authorization read sites workspace-wide. Fix is RFC compliance +
future-proofing.

[decision] decision.arch.irongate-thin-entrypoint — irongate-server main.rs is thin import+wrap; boot logic single-sourced in lib startup::run (status: todo, access: 0)
    DECISION: irongate-server main.rs is a thin import+wrap entrypoint; all boot
logic + production env validation is single-sourced in the irongate_auth lib.

CHOICE: main.rs = crate doc + #![forbid(unsafe_code)] + a #[tokio::main] that
calls irongate_auth::startup::boot() (a re-export of startup::run::run). The whole
boot sequence lives in the lib's startup::run module family (run.rs hub +
config/pools/router/serve children, each <=100 LOC). validate_production_env lives
in startup/env_validation/production.rs as the SINGLE source; main.rs no longer
carries any private duplicate of it (or of init_tracing / build_cors_layer /
shutdown_signal / health_check / gnap_discovery — all were verbatim shadows of
existing lib modules with zero non-self callers).

WHY: §STRUCTURAL_DISCIPLINE (main.rs = wire-up only) + §MICRO_FILE (<=100 LOC) +
single-source-of-truth for the boot contract (a CORS-policy or env-check edit can
no longer drift between two copies). Moving boot code from the lint-relaxed bin
into the strict lib also subjects it to the full workspace deny-block going
forward.

NAMING: module `run` + fn `run` collide as `run::run`; re-exported at the startup
hub as `boot` so the call site reads `irongate_auth::startup::boot()`.

LINT NOTE: serve() carries #[expect(clippy::cognitive_complexity, reason=...)] —
tokio::try_join! + 2 inline async gates macro-expand to a large poll state
machine (metric 59); the logic is linear. Sanctioned macro-inflation escape, same
as shutdown.rs's tokio::select! (rust-clippy#14417). NOT #[allow].

FILES: main.rs; startup.rs; startup/env_validation.rs (+production.rs);
startup/run.rs (+config.rs, pools.rs, router.rs, serve.rs).
SOURCE: §STRUCTURAL_DISCIPLINE, §MICRO_FILE_DISCIPLINE, §RUST_STRICT (#[expect]).

- purchase_requisitions(platform_id, requisition_number UNIQUE/platform, title, justification, suggested_vendor_id soft, estimated_amount_minor BIGINT CHECK>=0, status, needed_by, requested_by).
- supplier_scorecards(platform_id, vendor_id soft, period, on_time_rate_bps INT CHECK 0..10000, quality_score INT CHECK 0..100, total_orders BIGINT CHECK>=0, notes; UNIQUE platform+vendor+period).
- inbound_shipments(platform_id, purchase_order_id soft nullable, carrier, tracking_number, status, expected_arrival, received_qty BIGINT CHECK>=0; UNIQUE platform+carrier+tracking).
- RLS on all 3: owner/admin all + employee read, platform-scoped (mirrors mig 301).
All money = integer minor units (fintech-precision LAW). on_time as basis points (int), never float.

== PHASE 2 — attendance_clock (mig 324) ==
Consented, employee-INITIATED time tracking (workforce-monitoring skill: the
gold-standard signal tier — explicit employee action, never passive capture).
  - migration 324_ironcore_hrms_attendance.sql: attendance_shifts + enum
    attendance_shift_status{open,on_break,closed} + RLS. Neon ACID system-of-record
    (attendance is LOW-volume — Postgres is the correct tier, §DATA_TIER_SPLIT).
    Partial unique index `unique_open_shift_per_employee WHERE status<>'closed'`
    enforces one open shift (illegal-states-unrepresentable: double clock-in → 422).
    RLS self-rw for employee dashboard parity (workforce-monitoring §0.1); employee_id
    bound from auth.employee_id GUC (never client input — RLS WITH CHECK). jurisdiction
    stamp for retention/legal routing (§1). break_seconds integer (never float).
  - dto/attendance.rs (AttendanceResponse) · pdp/methods/timesheet.rs (allow_clock
    = timesheet:write, allow_read_timesheet = timesheet:read; canonical `timesheet`
    resource mig 259) · handlers/{shift_rows, clock_in, clock_out, break_punch,
    list_my_attendance}.
  - clock_out folds an in-progress break window into break_seconds atomically;
    break_punch is a single atomic CASE UPDATE (toggle). Wrong-state punches hit
    the state guard → RowNotFound → clock_state_error → precise 422 (no enumeration
    risk: employee acts on own shift). Concurrency-safe: the unique index makes each
    UPDATE single-row + the accumulator is one atomic statement (no FOR UPDATE needed).
  - 4 routes: POST /attendance/clock-in|clock-out|break, GET /attendance/me.

SECURITY HARDENING (gate-flagged P0, fixed at root, NOT suppressed):
  Dropped #[serde(default)] from ALL AdminRole fields. The RESPONSE_SECURITY gate
  correctly flagged #[serde(default)] on the is_system bool as privilege-by-
  omission (a missing field would silently deserialize to false). Even though this
  DTO is display-only (the backend enforces is_system=false guards on UPDATE/DELETE/
  set_role_permissions server-side, incl. FOR UPDATE row-lock), the STRICT contract
  is correct: the backend SELECT always returns all 4 columns, so a missing field
  is a contract violation that MUST fail to deserialize (-> .ok() -> None -> fail-
  closed loading), never silent-default. Proven by test
  missing_is_system_fails_closed_no_silent_default (asserts None, not Some{false}).

BACKEND: no change. admin::roles::list_roles already serves GET /api/admin/roles.
The whole roles sub-router is gated at iron_will_international_internal:roles:write
(admin/routes.rs:29-32), so a viewer lacking that primitive is denied -> the page's
fail-closed loading state covers it (denied == pending, anti-enumeration).

REAL BUG FIXED AT ROOT (§bug_lint_hunt, surfaced ONLY by the release bundle):
  platforms/jacobs-ladder-marketing/.../business_detail_content/reviews.rs:26 had
  `let key = refresh(); ... key: "{key}"`. Debug `cargo check` counted the read, but
  dx's release rsx codegen lowers the `key:` special attribute differently and the
  read on the intermediate binding is NOT registered → --deny=unused_variables fired
  only in the release bundle. FIX (not suppression, not deletion): inlined the signal
  directly — `key: "{refresh}"` (refresh already used via `refresh += 1`), matching
  the codebase-universal direct-interpolation idiom (20+ sites; reviews.rs was the
  lone `let x = ...; key: "{x}"` outlier). Behavior byte-identical (same component
  subscribes to the same signal; same re-mount on submit). reviews.rs now 40 LOC.

LESSON (captured as pattern.frontend.dioxus-release-rsx-key-unused-var): a passing
debug `cargo check --target wasm32` does NOT prove a clean `dx bundle --release` —
the release bundle is its own witness. Always run the bundle for a frontend-verify card.

prod-deploy (Pages/Workers/Container) remains OWNER-GATED (needs CF secrets).

[decision] decision.infra.outbox-poller-lease-claim-no-lock-across-publish-2026-06-10 — Outbox poller: lease-claim via last_attempt_at, publish OUTSIDE txn (fix lock-across-network pool exhaustion) (status: done, access: 0)
    FIX for roadmap.unit.bug.outbox-poller-http-in-open-txn. PRIOR: poll_once opened one txn, claimed rows FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, then awaited publisher::publish() (HTTP) for every row INSIDE the open txn -> pooled conn + row locks held across N network calls -> pool exhaustion + lock contention. CANONICAL outbox relay (research 2026): claim by a lease timestamp, RELEASE the lock (commit) BEFORE the network publish, mark sent only after broker confirms; lock-timeout/lease lets another relay reclaim safely. FIX (pure code, NO migration): reuse the EXISTING outbox.last_attempt_at column as the lease. Phase 1 short txn: UPDATE outbox SET last_attempt_at=NOW() WHERE id IN (SELECT ... WHERE published_at IS NULL AND retry_count<max AND (last_attempt_at IS NULL OR last_attempt_at < NOW()-CLAIM_LEASE) ORDER BY id LIMIT batch FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING ...; COMMIT (releases locks). Phase 2: publisher::publish() OUTSIDE any txn; per-row autocommit UPDATE sets published_at (success) or retry_count+last_error (fail). CLAIM_LEASE const = 60s (must exceed worst-case single-publish latency; rare lease-expiry reclaim is a benign duplicate — outbox is at-least-once + consumers idempotent). At-least-once preserved. SOURCE: decision.audit.system-bug-hunt-2026-06-10; outbox pattern (microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html).

[decision] decision.bug.auth-client-content-digest-rfc9421 — SignedClient RFC 9421 Content-Digest fix: BLAKE3 body signing, backend-parity format, serialize-once invariant (status: todo, access: 0)
    DECISION: SignedClient RFC 9421 httpsig now covers POST/PUT request bodies via a BLAKE3 Content-Digest signed component, closing a body-tamper integrity gap. Per §GNAP_NOT_OAUTH LAW: "PASETO + httpsig is the indivisible pair" and "Content-Digest on every protected call" — the body MUST be a covered component, not just @method/@target-uri.

BUG CLASS: incomplete httpsig coverage. The signer (apply_gnap_auth) never received the body bytes, so the signed base omitted the body entirely — a MITM/compromised-proxy body swap still verified. Structural root: the signature fn took only (method, path).

KEY CONTRACT (backend parity — verified by reading gnap-crypto):
- Digest algorithm: BLAKE3, format `blake3=:<base64(blake3(body).as_bytes())>:` — byte-identical to gnap-crypto::httpsig::helpers::compute_content_digest. NOT RFC 9530 SHA (§CRYPTO_INTERNAL_ONLY: we own both ends).
- Covered component name: "content-digest" (backend verify.rs:41 requires it in Signature-Input for POST/PUT/PATCH with a body, else ContentDigestNotCovered).
- Signature base line format: `"<component>": <value>` joined with '\n' (backend base.rs:57). Header name: Content-Digest (case-insensitive lookup).
- sig params now include alg="ed25519".

SERIALIZE-ONCE INVARIANT: post/put serialize the body via serde_json::to_vec ONCE and send those exact bytes with .body() (not reqwest .json(), which re-serializes and could yield a digest that doesn't match the transmitted bytes -> ContentDigestMismatch on the backend). This is the subtle correctness pin.

DESIGN CHOICES:
- blake3 1.5 added to auth-client (matches Backend pin); portable impl wasm32-safe (no SIMD/rayon).
- ApiError gains Serialization(#[from] serde_json::Error) — propagate, never swallow.
- digest helper lifted to its own digest.rs (§MICRO_FILE: internals.rs would exceed 100 LOC).
- send_bodied takes the verb-specific RequestBuilder (no method-string catch-all — RUST_GUARD bans `_ =>`).

VERIFY: cargo check + nextest 12/12 (5 new digest tests incl. mutated_body_produces_different_digest = the integrity proof). Fully closeable (client code, no live apply) -> status verified.

OUT-OF-SCOPE OBSERVATION (filed, not fixed): the frontend base omits the "@signature-params" line the backend always appends — a pre-existing base-format divergence orthogonal to Content-Digest. Worth a follow-up audit of whether this client is yet wired to the strict verifier.
SOURCE: RFC 9421 §2.1 (HTTP Message Signatures) https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9421.html · §GNAP_NOT_OAUTH (gnap-not-oauth.md) · Backend gnap-crypto httpsig {helpers,verify,base}.rs · auth-client/src/client/signed/{internals,verbs,digest}.rs
[decision] decision.bug.rainfire-contribution-toctou-328 — Rainfire contribution TOCTOU fix: migration 328 idempotency_key unique idx + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING dedup (status: todo, access: 0)
    DECISION: close the Rainfire contribution-creation TOCTOU by adding a DB-level idempotency anchor (migration 328: idempotency_key column + partial UNIQUE index) and switching create_contribution to INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING with a fallback SELECT.

BUG CLASS: check-then-act on uniqueness without a DB unique index (TOCTOU). SELECT-then-INSERT has an unavoidable race; the ONLY correct fix is to push uniqueness into the storage engine. The 24h completed-donation SELECT cannot help — it checks a different state (completed) and is itself racy.

WHY ON CONFLICT (not the prior NOW()-window approach): the old code comment claimed ON CONFLICT was "impossible" because the dedup predicate used NOW() (volatile, can't index). True for a TIME-WINDOW key — but the handler ALREADY computes a deterministic, immutable idempotency_key ("rf_donate_{mission}_{donor}_{client_key}", donate.rs). That key IS indexable. The fix threads that existing key into the row (it was previously used only at the payment-intent level) and indexes IT — sidestepping the NOW() problem entirely.

DESIGN:
- Partial UNIQUE index WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL: legacy pre-migration rows (NULL key) never collide; a NULL key stays allowed for any non-idempotent internal insert.
- Conflict = dedup hit, NOT error: fetch_optional returns None on conflict -> SELECT the existing row and return it, so a double-click gets the SAME contribution (and the same payment intent downstream), never a duplicate.
- create_contribution signature gained idempotency_key: &str; single caller (donate_payment.rs) updated.

CORRECTNESS: storage-engine-guaranteed. A UNIQUE index makes concurrent INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING atomic — exactly one writer wins, the rest get zero rows and fall to the SELECT. Canonical upsert-dedup; no application-level lock needed.

VERIFY: cargo check -p service-rainfire-missions exit 0; rg confirmed single caller; git diff +28/-9. Live concurrency nextest (N parallel -> 1 row) + migration apply are owner-gated (no scratch Postgres on host) -> AGENT_GATED on deploy.
SOURCE: contributions.rs create_contribution · donate.rs (idempotency_key derivation) · migrations_local/328_mission_contributions_idempotency.sql · Postgres ON CONFLICT https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-insert.html#SQL-ON-CONFLICT

[decision] decision.jacobs_ladder_marketing.jobs-i64-salary-and-list-embeds-attributes — JLM jobs port: i64 whole-unit salary + list DTO embeds typed attributes (status: done, access: 0)
    DECISION: jacobs_ladder_marketing jobs-vertical frontend port — money + list-row typing.

CHOICE 1 — Salary is i64 WHOLE currency units, never f64.
Rationale: §payment-precision LAW (i64 cents/units never f64). Jobs salary data
is integer (no sub-unit), so i64 whole-units is precision-exact. DTO fields
salary_min/salary_max: Option<i64>. Regression proof: salary_max 9007199254740993
(2^53+1) round-trips exactly (f64 would lose it). Frontend is precision-correct
regardless of the backend CREATE-request f64 defect (roadmap.unit.bug.jacobs-jobs-create-request-salary-f64-coercion, separately filed).

CHOICE 2 — Browse list DTO embeds typed attributes per row.
JobListingSummary { #[serde(flatten)] listing: ClassifiedListing, attributes: JobAttributes }.
Rationale: backend jobs list returns full per-row objects WITH attributes
(Vec<JacobsJobsOwnerResponse>); embedding attributes makes each grid card
compile-time-typed (illegal-states-unrepresentable — a row CANNOT exist without
its attributes) rather than re-parsing an untyped bag. classifieds_list_jobs ->
Vec<JobListingSummary> via ListEnvelope<JobListingSummary>.

API SURFACE (api-client::classifieds): classifieds_list_jobs, classifieds_get_job,
classifieds_create_job; DTOs JobAttributes, JobListingSummary, JobListingDetail, CreateJobBody.

SHELL: 3 Route variants (/classifieds/jobs/new, /:slug, bare browse), pages/jobs/{browse,detail,create}.rs.
Anti-enumeration: detail not-found + denied share one copy; create maps all errors to one string.

VERIFY: cargo check -p {api-client, platform-jacobs-ladder-marketing, shell-jacobs-ladder-marketing}
exit 0; nextest 415/415; all new files <=57 LOC (§MICRO_FILE).
[decision] decision.jacobs_ladder_marketing.jobs-create-request-salary-f64-to-decimal — jacobs-jobs create/update salary f64->Decimal (6th f64-money anti-pattern fix) (status: done, access: 0)
    DECISION: jacobs-jobs CreateJacobsJobsRequest + UpdateJacobsJobsRequest salary_min/max
changed Option<f64> -> Option<rust_decimal::Decimal>. 6th fixed instance of the
f64-money anti-pattern class.

ROOT CAUSE: read path (models/public.rs) already used Decimal (exact base-10 column),
but the CREATE/UPDATE request structs narrowed inbound salary JSON through binary f64
BEFORE the Decimal store — a read/write type-ASYMMETRY across the wire boundary. A
salary >2^53 (or 99999999.99) lost precision at deserialize, invisible to every
read-path test.

FIX: create_request.rs:50,52 + update_request.rs:23,25 -> Option<Decimal>; serde
deserializes a JSON number into Decimal exactly (no f64 intermediate). handlers/create.rs:92
non-negative check now compares against rust_decimal::Decimal::ZERO. core_models::Decimal
is `pub use rust_decimal::Decimal` (same type, confirmed core/models/lib.rs:26).

REGRESSION PROOF: models/create_request/tests.rs — salary_max_past_2pow53_deserializes_exact
asserts 9007199254740993 (2^53+1) round-trips exact; salary_max_with_cents_deserializes_exact
asserts 99999999.99 exact. nextest 2/2 PASS.

VERIFY: SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo check -p service-jacobs-ladder-marketing exit 0;
nextest 2/2; rg confirms zero f64 salary fields remain.

ANTI-PATTERN CLASS (f64-money, now 6 fixed): automotive-create price, rainfire raised/goal,
advertising bid, payment-service amount_to_cents, frontend automotive create form, +this.
RULE: money is NEVER f64 — i64 cents/whole-units OR rust_decimal::Decimal (§payment-precision LAW).
Geo coords (latitude/longitude) correctly stay f64 — NOT money.

[decision] decision.arch.audit-dual-store-postgres-spine-scylla-payload — Audit immutable records: Postgres = hash-chain spine + metadata; ScyllaDB = payload mapped by hash (status: done, access: 0)
    Owner directive 2026-06-17 (Dashboard P7 B3 scoping): immutable audit records split across two stores by role.

POSTGRES (core/audit, the ledger spine): METADATA ONLY — the BLAKE3 entry_hash + prev_hash chain links, plus transactional/reference data (id, event_type, actor_id, resource_id, action, created_at, sequence). Postgres remains the ordered, ACID, tamper-evident hash chain (compute_entry_hash + verify_chain stay here). The current AuditEntry.metadata jsonb payload column is the part that MOVES to Scylla.

SCYLLADB (new audit keyspace, migrations_scylla/NNN_platform_audit*.cql): the ACTUAL immutable record payload (the bulk content / full metadata blob), keyed/mapped BY entry_hash. High-write immutable content store; Postgres entry_hash is the foreign key into Scylla.

PATTERN: Postgres = ordered ACID hash-chain ledger (FK = hash); Scylla = immutable content store keyed by hash. Mirrors existing project seam: core/audit/chain.rs already computes entry_hash; Scylla bringup proven (#1423-1426, migrations_scylla 001-010, multiple *-scylla crates, scylla-tls).

B3 audit-trail-api IMPACT: no longer plain Postgres read. Flow = read hash+metadata rows from Postgres (get_entries_by_actor/resource + verify_chain) -> resolve full payload from Scylla by entry_hash. Needs: (1) Scylla audit keyspace + table (partition by entry_hash or actor+bucket), (2) dual-store audit repo, (3) append path writes spine to PG + payload to Scylla atomically (outbox/2-phase consideration — loophole: PG commit + Scylla write must not orphan). 

B2 metrics-api: still unresolved (no queryable metrics store; OTel = spans to external collector, waf metrics.rs = push scrape). Deferred pending owner source decision.

§CRYPTO: hash is BLAKE3 (internal). §HYPERDRIVE_RLS on PG audit reads. §MICRO_FILE on new repo.

[decision] decision.arch.black-diamond-fire-seller-support-substrate — Black Diamond Fire seller-support substrate: reuse core_comms thread rails (not Scylla/chat, not a 3rd substrate) (status: todo, access: 0)
    BDF seller-support — PLAN (substrate + architecture) authored 2026-06-10. IMPLEMENT owner-gated.

Spec parent: decision.arch.black-diamond-fire-standalone-platform (point 4: direct seller support).
Roadmap: roadmap.unit.platform.black-diamond-fire.seller-support.

OWNER MODEL: the customer contacts the SELLER directly, NOT Iron Will International.
IWI = platform rails only; sellers are autonomous operators. IWI is NOT in the support
loop by default (escalation to IWI = a FUTURE explicit policy decision, never the default).

== SUBSTRATE DECISION (the card's "pick ONE at plan time", reuse-first) ==
SELECTED: partner-comms / core_comms thread rails. REJECTED: chat-service/Scylla rails.
REJECTED: authoring any third messaging substrate (banned by card + owner no-duplication law).

WHY core_comms (scored, reuse-first):
- core_comms already ships the exact primitives: thread-per-relationship + BLAKE3 audit
  chain + PII redaction — PROVEN in iwi-partner-comms (partner↔IWI) and JLM partner-reply.
  Buyer↔seller support is structurally the SAME: a durable, audited, PII-sensitive
  BUSINESS thread, low-to-moderate volume, dispute-resolution-grade record.
- Neon-backed (ACID/transactional) — correct durability for support + the BLAKE3 chain is
  exactly the tamper-evident trail a seller-dispute system needs.
- chat-service/Scylla rails are built for HIGH-VOLUME REAL-TIME chat (Soundbak DMs, DO WS,
  E2E double-ratchet). E2E encryption would HINDER seller triage + dispute audit (the
  seller MUST read; a future IWI-escalation policy needs a readable history). Wrong
  properties + overkill for support threads.
- The JLM partner-reply precedent proves the reuse pattern: core_comms rails + a
  platform-specific participant-pairing + ABAC binding layer (NOT a fork of the substrate).

== THREAD SHAPE ==
Thread key: (order_id | listing_id, buyer_id, seller_org_id). One thread per
buyer×seller×(order|listing). Buyer entry: "Contact seller" on any sellable item (BDF
ecommerce item OR catalog-bridged JLM listing). Seller inbox: BDF seller portal
(shared-SPA skeleton). Messages + attachments reuse core_comms message/attachment rails.

== ABAC (NOW EXPRESSIBLE) ==
Primitives: black_diamond_fire:support_thread:{read,write,close}.
DEPENDENCY MET: roadmap.unit.infra.matrix-platforms-add-black-diamond-fire is DONE — the
black_diamond_fire matrix_platforms axis row has shipped, so BDF primitives are no longer
inexpressible (the §ABAC_MATRIX CLAUDE.md "row MISSING" note is now stale; its own unblock
condition is satisfied). Live mig-apply of the axis row remains owner-gated like all
mig-applies, but the primitive is now CODEABLE.
Scopes: seller = own-org threads (assigned/department); buyer = own threads (own); IWI =
NONE by default (no IWI read/write — the whole point of seller-direct support).

== REUSE PLAN (IMPLEMENT, owner-gated) ==
- core_comms: thread + message + attachment + BLAKE3 chain + PII redaction (as-is).
- NEW (BDF-specific, thin): participant-pairing (buyer, seller_org) + BDF ABAC binding +
  seller-portal inbox UI + buyer "Contact seller" entry. Mirrors JLM partner-reply's
  thin reuse layer. NO new substrate, NO core_comms fork.

== STATUS / GATING ==
PLAN: authored (this decision). IMPLEMENT: OWNER-GATED — the card is explicit
("owner-gated like all BDF builds; do NOT auto-build"; PLAN → owner greenlight → IMPLEMENT).
Per §PLAN_TO_KAVACH (2026-06-10), implementation when greenlit is by Claude Code (NOT
Cursor — the card's "IMPLEMENT (Cursor)" line predates the Cursor retirement). The card is
parked OWNER-GATED, not done (full DoD = implement+test+harden awaits greenlight).
[decision] decision.arch.per-platform-independent-ingress — Per-platform INDEPENDENT ingress — NO BFF, NO single API gateway, NO waf-ingress Worker; frontend api-client calls each microservice directly; in-process middleware is the sole app-layer protection (no double layer) (status: done, access: 0)
    DEPENDS_ON: nicole-carpenter/decision/ACID
DECISION (owner-directed 2026-06-19, clarified 2026-07-01): per-platform INDEPENDENT north-south ingress — NO BFF, NO single API gateway, NO waf-ingress Worker. Each separated microservice exposes its OWN client-reachable API directly.

NO-BFF / NO-SINGLE-API (owner directive 2026-07-01): there is NO Backend-for-Frontend and NO single aggregating gateway. The backend is fully separated microservices; the frontend api-client calls EACH microservice's own API endpoint DIRECTLY (per-platform base-URL / per-platform CNAME, e.g. jlm-api.ironwillinternational.com). No client request fans through one dispatcher. REJECT re-introducing a BFF, a same-origin aggregation proxy, or a single gateway.

PROBLEM (historical): every client request once entered through iron-will-api (sole north-south gateway). iron-will-api down => ALL platforms dark — a true SPOF.

DECISION: each platform gets its OWN client-reachable CF edge ingress (own route/custom_domain) bound DIRECTLY to that platform's Container-Worker (env.<SERVICE>.fetch(req)). One platform's ingress failing leaves the others fully serving. iron-will-api is ONE ingress among many (IronCore ERP + auth/media/admin + cross-platform partner-comms/feedback/commerce-returns), NOT the dispatcher.

NO-DOUBLE-LAYER / WAF-INGRESS REMOVED (owner directive 2026-07-01): the standalone waf-ingress Worker / loopback binary is COMPLETELY REMOVED from the backend (folds dep.waf-ingress.loopback-vs-service-binding). App-layer protection lives ONCE, in-process, in the service middleware — GNAP + RFC 9421 httpsig verify (core/auth/src/middleware/signature_middleware.rs) + input sanitize (core/utils/sanitize.rs). That middleware IS the security boundary. Cloudflare-native edge WAF is a platform capability at the edge (not our code, not a second app-layer we author). Do NOT reintroduce a WAF Worker / proxy hop — that is the banned double layer; the middleware already has those protections.

SCOPE: NORTH-SOUTH ingress only.

REJECTED — per-platform DATABASE isolation: CONTRAINDICATED. Shared ONE Neon DB is intentional/load-bearing (arch.db.single-neon-irongate-schema: 302 cross-platform FKs; mesh money-paths e3 JLM->RFM commission, e4 Soundbak->JLM attribution, e6 Soundbak->RFM donation need ACID in ONE txn). NEVER re-litigate: DB stays single.

CANON COMPLIANCE: no new backend crate (ingress = thin CF Worker TS shim, not Rust) per arch.invariant.no-new-backend-refine-only. Auth NOT bypassed — each platform ingress forwards to a service that re-verifies GNAP + httpsig in-process. East-west stays async via outbox + CF Queues (core/comms/src/outbox.rs) — UNCHANGED.

REUSABLE: deploy/<svc>/{wrangler.jsonc,src/index.ts} @cloudflare/containers Container+getContainer shim (binding pattern e.g. JACOBS_LADDER_MARKETING_SERVICE); core/auth signature_middleware; outbox.

SOURCE: owner directive 2026-06-19 + 2026-07-01 clarification (no BFF, no single API, waf-ingress removed, no double layers) · arch.invariant.cloudflare-service-bindings-mesh · dep.waf-ingress.loopback-vs-service-binding.

[decision] decision.deploy.smoke-test-axum-root-nest-panic-fix — DEPLOY-DEPENDENCY FOUND+FIXED by smoke test: core/health bootstrap.rs:239 nest("/") → axum 0.8 BOOT PANIC (all 14 containers); fixed to merge(); live /health 200, 37k-110k req/s (status: done, access: 0)
    SMOKE TEST 2026-06-18 (local, BDF service binary): found a DEPLOY-gating runtime panic that cargo check/clippy/nextest ALL missed (type-valid, panics at router construction). core/health/src/bootstrap.rs:239 used Router::nest("/", app_router) — axum 0.8 FORBIDS root-nesting: panics 'Nesting at the root is no longer supported. Use merge instead.' on boot. Since ALL 14 containers route through core_health::bind_with_lazy_db, EVERY container would have crash-looped on startup in the preview deploy. FIX: nest("/") -> merge(app_router) (axum 0.8 migration; merge flattens routes at root = the intended behavior). 3-witness: rebuild Finished 52.95s; live launch → GET /health = HTTP 200 {"status":"ok"} (boot panic gone); the DATABASE_URL -pooler ERROR in log is CORRECT cf-compat LazyResource behavior (health binds before DB, fails-soft, still serves). BENCHMARK (ab keep-alive, live /health): c=1 = 0.027ms/req (37k req/s); c=50 = 0.455ms mean, p99 1ms, 110k req/s. (~20-55 failed of 30-50k = ab keep-alive teardown races, <0.1%, not server errors.) LESSON: 'it compiled + tests pass' ≠ 'it boots' — only a running smoke test caught this; add a boot-smoke step to CI before wrangler upload. SOURCE: smoke test this session · axum 0.8 router migration · §evidence_over_inference.
