[decision] decision.security.gap-sweep-insights-awareness-2026-07-03 — AWARENESS: 5 cross-cutting security insights (fail-closed defaults · forbid-lint=bug-class · shared-layer-not-per-service · boot-read secrets · timeouts-both-ends); meta: absence-bugs (status: done, access: 0)
    Spec parent: arch.stack

AWARENESS: 5 cross-cutting security insights from the 2026-07-03 backend gap sweep.
These are the DURABLE PATTERNS behind the findings — an author self-enforces these so
the whole CLASS never recurs (not just the specific site). Raw findings live in
[[decision.security.backend-gap-sweep-2026-07-03]]. Companion:
[[decision.arch.payment-dashboard-url-centralized-config-2026-06-20]],
[[audit.centralized-config-payment-wallet-drift-2026-06-20]].

INSIGHT 1 — FAIL-CLOSED IS A DEFAULT-VALUE DISCIPLINE, NOT JUST A CODE PATH.
The CRIT cookie bug (session.rs:111) was a boolean DEFAULT: is_production()=false when
ENVIRONMENT is unset → Secure flag dropped. The security property inverted on the
ABSENCE of config, silently. RULE: any security-bearing default (is_prod, is_auth_ready,
visibility, allow/deny) MUST default to the SAFE side when its input is unset/unknown.
"Unknown → treat as production/secure/deny." Grep target: `Err(_) => false` /
`unwrap_or(false)` on a security flag. This mirrors the fail-closed pattern already used
correctly at CORS (user-service/cors.rs:80-95 hard-errors when ALLOWED_ORIGINS unset).

INSIGHT 2 — A MISSING `forbid` LINT IS A WHOLE BUG CLASS LEFT OPEN.
§RUST_STRICT forbids unwrap/expect/panic — so those bugs can't compile. But
arithmetic_side_effects is NOT forbidden, so raw +/-/* on money i64 compiles, and the
sweep found 5 sites (money.rs:38 HIGH + 4 more). The lint gap = the bug class. RULE:
when a defect class is mechanically detectable by a clippy lint, ADD THE LINT to
[workspace.lints] (forbid/deny) rather than fixing sites one-by-one — the compiler
becomes the reviewer. Candidate additions: arithmetic_side_effects (money safety),
indexing_slicing (already), lossy casts. A longer manual fix list is not a fix; the
lint is.

INSIGHT 3 — CROSS-CUTTING PROTECTIONS MUST BE A SHARED LAYER, NOT PER-SERVICE COPIES.
The sweep found the SAME gap three times from drift: 16/20 services lack TimeoutLayer,
11/20 lack security headers, per-service headers.rs/cors.rs/csrf.rs duplication. A
protection that each of ~20 services must remember to wire WILL be forgotten by some.
RULE (§CENTRALIZED_CONFIG generalized to middleware): baseline protections — timeout,
body-limit, security headers, CORS, CSRF — belong in ONE shared router-builder every
service composes, so a new service inherits the floor by construction, cannot ship
without it. Per-service opt-in is drift-by-design.

INSIGHT 4 — READ SECRETS ONCE AT BOOT; A REQUEST-TIME env read FAILS IN PRODUCTION.
7 sites read env at request time, 3 of them SECRETS (INTERNAL_KEY, INTROSPECT_SECRET,
CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL_API_TOKEN). A missing/rotated secret then fails on a LIVE user request
under load, not at the deploy you watch. RULE (§CENTRALIZED_CONFIG, already LAW): every
env var via a typed config fragment read ONCE at boot; a request-path std::env::var is a
P0. This insight is the LAW's WHY — fail-at-boot converts a prod incident into a deploy
incident you see instantly.

INSIGHT 5 — TIMEOUTS ARE THE FORGOTTEN DoS DEFENSE; SET THEM AT BOTH ENDS.
The CRIT: no per-request TimeoutLayer on 16 services AND external clients (Nominatim
zip_cache.rs:38-42) with connect_timeout but no request .timeout(). A hung upstream or
slow client ties up a worker indefinitely — the cheapest DoS. RULE: EVERY inbound router
gets a TimeoutLayer(30s); EVERY outbound reqwest client gets BOTH connect_timeout AND a
full request .timeout(). Centralize the outbound side in core/utils/src/http.rs so all
internal callers inherit it (OWASP API4 Unrestricted Resource Consumption).

META-INSIGHT: 4 of 5 classes are "absence" bugs — a missing lint, a missing layer, a
missing timeout, a missing boot-read, an unsafe default. Security regressions here come
from what is NOT wired, not what is wrong. The systemic fix is to make the safe thing the
DEFAULT (shared layer, forbid lint, fail-closed default) so absence = safe, not exposed.

SOURCE: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0x11-t10/
SOURCE: fail-closed default — verified session.rs:33,111 (this session).
SOURCE: §RUST_STRICT (rust-strict-no-suppression.md) · §CENTRALIZED_CONFIG (centralized-config.md).
[decision] decision.arch.keyset-cursor-pagination-shared — Keyset-cursor pagination + filter + sort as shared core module for all ~30 list endpoints (owner directive 2026-07-03); LIMIT caps are interim floor (status: done, access: 0)
    Spec parent: arch.stack

DECISION: keyset-cursor pagination + filter + sort as a SHARED module for all list endpoints.
Trigger: owner directive 2026-07-03 "We need Proper Pagination and Cursor here to Handle
Filtering, SORTING" — supersedes the interim LIMIT-cap H3 fix.
Cross-ref: [[decision.security.backend-gap-sweep-2026-07-03]] H3 (unbounded lists),
[[roadmap.unit.security.post-endpoint-hardening]].

SCOPE (owner-chosen): ALL ~30 flagged fetch_all list endpoints, via ONE reusable core
helper (§CENTRALIZED_CONFIG generalized — shared, not per-site). First 2 consumers:
ironcore-internal list_purchase_orders.rs, user-service drafts.rs.

STYLE (owner-chosen): KEYSET (cursor), NOT offset. Rationale: O(page) via index not
O(offset) scan; stable under concurrent inserts (offset skips/dupes rows); no deep-offset
scan cost. Cursor = opaque base64 of the last row's (sort_col, id) tuple.
SOURCE: https://use-the-index-luke.com/no-offset (keyset pagination canonical).
SOURCE: OWASP API4:2023 https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa4 (bounded lists).

DESIGN (from architect LLD):
- Cursor: opaque base64 of (sort_key, id); decode-failure → first page (tamper-tolerant, not error).
- PageParams { limit (capped), cursor, sort, filter } request DTO.
- Page<T> { items, next_cursor } response envelope; fetch n+1 to detect next page.
- SortKey ALLOWLIST enum — sort column NEVER a raw user string (ORDER BY injection guard);
  filter values $N-bound.
- keyset SQL builder: WHERE (sort_col, id) < ($cursor) ORDER BY sort_col DESC, id DESC LIMIT n+1.

INTERIM STATE (already shipped this session): LIMIT 500 (purchase_orders) + LIMIT 200 (drafts)
caps are the DoS FLOOR — cursor pagination REPLACES them with a page-size + next_cursor so
capped-out rows remain reachable. Caps stay until each endpoint migrates.

STATUS: LLD in review (diagram-first). Implementation = new roadmap unit
roadmap.unit.pagination.keyset-shared-module (P0 consumers first, then roll to ~30).
Constraints: §RUST_STRICT, §MICRO_FILE (≤100 LOC hub+leaf), §FULL_PLATFORM_SLUG.

    DEPENDS_ON: nicole-carpenter/decision/orchestrator

[decision] decision.gate.research-first-algo-hunter-deadlock-2026-07-04 — PROVEN gate defect: on an ALGO_HUNTER-flagged file, RESEARCH_FIRST (needs SOURCE: in file) and ALGO_HUNTER (forbids provenance comment in file) are mutually exclusive — kavach-rs algo_guard fix needed (status: done, access: 0)
    EXECUTION-PROVEN 2026-07-04 (not inferred): splitting ui-organisms notification_inbox logic/group.rs (grouping/filter/icon helpers ALGO_HUNTER flags as algorithmic) is unsatisfiable:
- Write WITH // SOURCE: url -> ALGO_HUNTER blocks: \"do NOT write any provenance comment\".
- Write WITHOUT it -> RESEARCH_FIRST blocks: \"cite a SOURCE: url in the write\".
- // kavach:intentional does NOT satisfy RESEARCH_FIRST (needs a literal SOURCE:/url string).
- ALGO decision row (decision.algo.notification-grouping-single-pass-2026-07-04) + fresh WebSearch in turn cache do NOT satisfy RESEARCH_FIRST (it wants the marker IN the file bytes).
The two gate predicates cannot both be true in one file. Proven by 3 direct write attempts.

ROOT FIX (kavach-rs algo_guard/check.rs, per session PRACTICE_DELTA): ALGO_HUNTER must ACCEPT a single // SOURCE: url line as satisfying provenance (not reject it), OR RESEARCH_FIRST must accept the recorded ALGO decision row / turn-cache research as the citation for an ALGO_HUNTER-flagged file. Same class as COMMENT_BLOAT<->RESEARCH_FIRST fixed 2026-06-30.

AGENT-DONE (landed clean, crate compiles): the 3 NON-algorithmic split files (types.rs, time.rs via doc-summary carve-out) are writable; only group.rs (ALGO_HUNTER-flagged) is deadlocked. Reverted to keep crate green (no half-split).

NOT bypassed: no gate disabled, no --no-verify, no guessed suppression. Blocker is real + proven; fix is in kavach-rs which the agent cannot edit from this repo.

CONSUMER: [[roadmap.unit.fe.notification-inbox-test-lift-algohunter-blocked]] + [[roadmap.unit.soundbak-social-service-microfile-compliance]] (same ALGO_HUNTER class on their algorithmic files).

[decision] decision.algo.notification-grouping-single-pass-2026-07-04 — Notification grouping: O(n) single-pass bucket-by-TimeGroup (Today/ThisWeek/Earlier) over per-item get_time_group; no sort needed since 3 fixed buckets (status: done, access: 0)
    ALGO CHOICE for group_notifications (ui-organisms notification_inbox logic/group.rs).

PROBLEM_CLASS: grouping/bucketing.
CHOSEN: single-pass O(n) partition into 3 fixed buckets (Today/ThisWeek/Earlier) by get_time_group(item.created_at, now), then emit non-empty buckets in fixed display order.
TIME: O(n) | SPACE: O(n).
REJECTED: (1) sort-then-group O(n log n) — unnecessary, only 3 fixed buckets, order is fixed not data-derived; (2) HashMap<TimeGroup,Vec> O(n) — same complexity but adds hash overhead + non-deterministic iteration needing a re-sort for display order; the 3 explicit Vecs are simpler + deterministic.
Related: filter_notifications O(n) linear filter (all passes through); unread_by_type O(n) HashMap count. type_icon/type_colors/group_label are O(1) match lookups (not algorithmic — fixed enumeration).
SOURCE: legacy dashboard NotificationInbox.tsx grouped-memo (port parity); civil-days epoch conversion howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html.
YEAR: 2026 | SEARCHED: 2026-07.
